verses.english: Linked Discourses 11.18
Chapter Two
Who Sakka Worships
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: “bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo mātaliṁ saṅgāhakaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: “Once upon a time, mendicants, Sakka, lord of gods, addressed his chariot handler Mātali,

verses.pali: ‘yojehi, samma mātali, sahassayuttaṁ ājaññarathaṁ. Uyyānabhūmiṁ gacchāma subhūmiṁ dassanāyā’ti.
verses.english: ‘My dear Mātali, harness the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds. We will go to a park and see the scenery.’

verses.pali: ‘Evaṁ, bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā sahassayuttaṁ ājaññarathaṁ yojetvā sakkassa devānamindassa paṭivedesi:
verses.english: ‘Yes, lord,’ replied Mātali. He harnessed the chariot and informed Sakka,
‘Good fellow, the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds has been harnessed.
Please go at your convenience.’

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vejayantapāsādā orohanto añjaliṁ katvā sudaṁ puthuddisā namassati.
verses.english: Then Sakka descended from the Palace of Victory, raised his cupped palms, and revered the various quarters.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: So Mātali the chariot handler addressed Sakka in verse:
‘Those proficient in the three Vedas worship you,
as do all the aristocrats on earth,
the four great kings,
and the glorious host of Thirty.
So what’s the name of the spirit
that you worship, Sakka?’
‘Those proficient in the three Vedas worship me,
as do all the aristocrats on earth,
the four great kings,
and the glorious host of Thirty.
But I revere those accomplished in ethics,
who have long trained in immersion,
who have rightly gone forth
for the culmination of spiritual life.
I also worship those householders,
the ethical lay followers
who make merit, Mātali,
providing for a partner in a principled manner.’
‘Those who you worship
seem to be the best in the world, Sakka.
I too will worship
those who you worship, Sakka.’
After saying this, Maghavā the chief,
king of gods, Sujā’s husband,
having worshiped the various quarters
climbed into his chariot.”
